results.title: Reviu: The review app for code your agent writes | Product Hunt
results.content:
Title: Reviu: The review app for code your agent writes | Product Hunt
### Trending products. The per-turn diff receipt is exactly the right idea. Sending a comment straight back to the agent with file and line context closes the loop without leaving the app. Would love the GitHub layer in the free tier, and a heads-up when a later turn edits a file I already marked as reviewed. Reviu stands out because the review is the product, not a panel bolted onto a chat, and the diffs are tied to agent turns rather than the whole branch. The “later turn touched something I already reviewed” case is exactly the kind of boundary Reviu is meant to make visible. Being able to comment on one exact line and send it back to the agent with the file and line attached is so much better than typing "fix that thing in the function" .... The useful unit is the turn: what changed, why, and can I reply on the exact line. "checkpoint or undo turns" is the feature I actually want - I've had claude code sessions where turn 4 did something I wanted to keep but turn 7 went off the rails and I had to manually untangle which file changes belonged to which turn. question on the undo though: if a turn already ran a shell command with a side effect outside the repo (hit an API, wrote to a db, pushed somewhere), does undo just revert the file diff and leave you to clean up the side effect yourself, or does it track that boundary too. @joris\_gallot that makes sense as a boundary, but it means the diff receipt can show a clean undo while a db write or an api call from that same turn is still sitting out there live. Our worst agent-written bug was a spend function that looked fine in the diff, it was writing bad balance events that only surfaced three tables away, and we missed it because we reviewed the whole branch squashed instead of turn by turn. The thing I'd want to know is what happens when a later turn edits a file I already marked reviewed.

results.content:
Title: Reviu: The review app for code your agent writes | Product Hunt
# Reviu. ## The review app for code your agent writes. Reviu is a native desktop app for reviewing agent-written code before you push. Run Claude Code, Codex, Gemini and other ACP agents in durable sessions, inspect every diff, send comments back to the agent, then stage, rebase, commit, open PRs and review GitHub pull requests without leaving the app. ## ReviuLaunches. ReviuThe review app for code your agent writes. Launched on October 5th, 2026. ReviuA rust desktop Git client for local Git and GitHub workflow. Launched on April 13th, 2026. used Reviu to build Incredible. #### What's great. The per-turn diff receipt is exactly the right idea. When an agent changes code across several files, reviewing turn by turn instead of one big squash diff catches things you'd otherwise miss. Sending a comment straight back to the agent with file and line context closes the loop without leaving the app. #### What needs improvement. Would love the GitHub layer in the free tier, and a heads-up when a later turn edits a file I already marked as reviewed. #### vs Alternatives. I already review agent-written code in Cursor and plain git diffs. Reviu stands out because the review is the product, not a panel bolted onto a chat, and the diffs are tied to agent turns rather than the whole branch. Thanks Fredric, really appreciate it! The “later turn touched something I already reviewed” case is exactly the kind of boundary Reviu is meant to make visible. GitHub in free is tougher because of API/auth/maintenance costs, but I want the local review loop to stay strong without Pro.

Title: Replit's AI Agent Website Builder - Honest Review : Replit Discussion Forums | Product Hunt
# Replit's AI Agent Website Builder - Honest Review. The Agent is good, if you want to build something insanely basic. Like an EdTech landing page, or an one pager for validating an idea. I tried to build an AI Agent that manages private keys and signs transactions for users. Replit for some reason created an app with the following things 1. I burned through a bunch of checkpoints trying to get a simple button (kept seeing a blank screen), and eventually started over and it just worked. The promise here is incredible - I think in a few months even, many non-coders will be able to create pretty robust applications. With greater power comes greater imagination...I think we might see an explosion of consumer app creativity as people build apps for themselves and a rare few take off. I think the great use case here is for the non-coders, and for the coders who want fast boilerplate and then go crazy. I used v0.dev from Vercel today and In like 30 seconds i got a nextJS dashboard with responsive UI in a second to use as a base for my new project. As a v1, I think the @Replit agent is one of the most impressive things in AI today. I agree that it gets confused with more complex tasks but I think in a few years (or sooner), it's going to be able to handle a surprising amount of tasks. And yeah it is a very well written software dont get me wrong. Is just, not the best thing, to see the whole world going bananas for software that will "might be good in a few years." We need to focus on current problems. we have a lot of stuff to build. I wasn't aware that replit has an AI agent to build website. Before it was paid, an agent to kick off a repo, but now is a website builder one. I agree that it is not there yet, but that could change 3 months from now. Replit Agent is an AI-powered tool on Replit Core or Teams that helps users build software from natural language prompts.
